record.context_brief: Infinite multiplicity in dimensions up to 6
record.original_question: For the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega subset of R^N with u = 0 on partial Omega, are there infinitely many sign-changing solutions when the dimension satisfies N <= 6?

evidence.quote: In [54], Schechter and Zou proved that for N >= 7, lambda > 0 there are infinitely many sign-changing solutions.
Open question 4: In a general bounded domain, are there infinitely many sign-changing solutions when N <= 6?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N\in\{3,4,5,6\}$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$ denote the critical Sobolev exponent. For $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$-\Delta u=\lambda u+|u|^{2^*-2}u\ \text{in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\ \text{on }\partial\Omega.$$
A weak solution $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ is called sign-changing (nodal) if both $u^+=\max\{u,0\}$ and $u^-=\max\{-u,0\}$ are nontrivial.

Question: For every $\lambda$ in the range for which the problem admits nontrivial solutions (in particular for all $\lambda>0$ below the relevant threshold), does the above problem possess infinitely many sign-changing solutions in $H^1_0(\Omega)$, for every bounded smooth domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ when $N\le 6$?
artifact.status_search_result: For N ≥ 7, Schechter–Zou established infinitely many sign-changing solutions for all λ > 0. For low dimensions N ∈ {4,5,6}, only finitely many solutions (at least N+1 pairs, by Devillanova–Solimini and Clapp–Weth) are known, with no information on their nodal nature. Recent works (e.g., on dimension six) explicitly list this as an open question, and the problem of whether infinitely many sign-changing solutions exist on a general bounded domain when N ≤ 6 remains open.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis-Nirenberg problems: Open questions and new results in dimension six
status_evidence.snippet: new results on the Brézis-Nirenberg problem in dimension six and lists some open questions
status_evidence.claim: Existence of infinitely many sign-changing solutions in low dimensions remains listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Infinitely many sign-changing solutions for the Brézis-Nirenberg problem
status_evidence.snippet: For N >= 7 there are infinitely many sign-changing solutions
status_evidence.claim: The infinite multiplicity result is established for N ≥ 7, leaving N ≤ 6 unresolved.
